figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. Regulation of glycosyltransferase enhances the synthesis of taxadiene in S. cerevisiae. tHMG1, N-terminally truncated HMG-CoA reductase 1; GGPP, 
geranylgeranyl diphosphate; ERG20, bifunctional (2E,6E)-farnesyl diphosphate; BST1, farnesyl transferase; TS, taxadiene synthase; and GGOH, geranylgeraniol.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. Effects of endogenous glycosyltransferase knockout on taxadiene synthesis in S. cerevisiae. (A) Schematic diagram of blocking glycosyltransferase in 
S. cerevisiae. (B) Effects of blocking glycosyltransferase activity on taxadiene production. In the control strains and single knockout strains of endogenous glyco­
syltransferases alg3, alg6, mnn11, and och1, the glycosyltransferase single knockout strains yZCL080, yZCL103, yZCL104, yZCL105, and yZCL106 for taxadiene 
synthesis were successfully constructed by introducing the single-copy pZCL106 plasmid related to taxadiene synthesis. **P < 0.01, *P < 0.05, based on Student's 
t-test.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. N-glycosylated proteomic analysis of the effects of mnn11 knockout on the taxadiene synthesis pathway. (A) Differential protein volcano map be­
tween the mnn11 glycosyltransferase gene knockout (Δmnn11) group yZCL105 and the control group yZCL080. (B) Statistical analysis of proteins with significantly 
different glycosylation levels between the Δmnn11 and control groups. (C) Analysis of the regulatory mechanisms underlying the differential glycosylation of 
proteins. (D) Western blot analysis of the differences in the expression levels of the taxadiene synthase (TS) protein between the control strain yZCL080 and the 
Δmnn11 strain yZCL105. Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) represents the internal reference protein band. The red arrows represent intact TS 
protein bands.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4. Multi-copy integration enhanced TS expression and GGPP synthesis precursor supply to improve the yield of taxadiene. (A) Schematic of the TS and 
G418 co-expression cassette at the Ty2 multi-copy site of the yeast genome. (B) Screening of high-yielding taxadiene using G418 concentration gradient. **P < 0.01, 
*P < 0.05, based on Student's t-test. (C) Western blot analysis of the differences in the expression levels of the TS protein between the control strain yZCL105 and the 
single knockout strain yZCL143 of the mnn11 glycosyltransferase gene. Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) represents the internal reference 
protein band. The red arrows represent intact TS protein bands. (D) Gray values of the intact TS protein in the control strain yZCL105 (intact TS/action, 14.2 %) and 
the single knockout strain yZCL143 of the mnn11 glycosyltransferase gene (intact TS/action, 68.9 %).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5. GGPP synthesis precursor supply to improve the yield of taxadiene. (A) Schematic of the Delta22, HO, TKL2, and YL1062W sites in the yeast genome 
integrating the GGPP precursor pathway. (B) Enhanced expression of the critical genes involved in the GGPP synthesis pathway increased taxadiene production. **P 
< 0.01, *P < 0.05, based on Student's t-test.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 6. Fed-batch fermentation of strain yZCL146 in a 5-L bioreactor. Fed-batch fermentations were performed at a 2.0 L scale using yeast extrac­
t–peptone–dextrose (YPD) medium and the engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain yZCL146. Optical density at 600 nm (OD600) was measured, and calibration 
curves were drawn for glucose, ethanol, and taxadiene during the fed-batch fermentation. Black arrows indicate the addition of n-dodecane and galactose to the 
medium. Error bars represent the means ± standard deviation from three biological replicates.
